about: The test portal's example queries, shown on /docs. Each names the profile it is for (from warden.example.yaml) and what sql-warden does with it: allowed, failed (allowed, but the database fails to run it) or the refusal code. tests/integration/test_portal_on_postgres.py checks every one against the seeded warehouse.

examples.title: A simple select
examples.sql: select id, name, price_cents from products order by id
examples.look: The Decision panel: parse, shape and access all pass, and a LIMIT 101 is added.

examples.title: A join and an aggregate
examples.sql:
select p.name, sum(o.quantity) as sold
from orders o join products p on p.id = o.product_id
group by p.name order by sold desc limit 10

examples.title: A LIMIT above the row cap is lowered
examples.sql: select id from orders limit 5000
examples.look: The rewrite note, and the Results footer saying the rows were cut off.

examples.title: Comments never reach the database
examples.sql: select name from products where id = 7 /* ; delete from orders */
examples.look: The SQL that ran: regenerated from the checked query, without the comment.

examples.title: A profile that may read everything
examples.sql: select title, count(*) from employee_salaries group by title order by title
examples.look: Press Compare: public may not read this table.

examples.title: DELETE
examples.sql: delete from orders

examples.title: Stacked statements
examples.sql: select 1; delete from orders

examples.title: A data-modifying CTE
examples.sql:
with gone as (delete from orders returning *)
select count(*) from gone

examples.title: FOR UPDATE
examples.sql: select id from orders for update

examples.title: pg_sleep
examples.sql: select pg_sleep(60)

examples.title: SQL hidden in a string
examples.sql: select query_to_xml('select * from employee_salaries', true, true, '')

examples.title: A function that isn't standard SQL
examples.sql: select age(created_at) from customers
examples.look: The reason says how to allow it: shape.allowed_functions in warden.yaml.

examples.title: Too many joins
examples.sql:
select count(*)
from orders o
join customers c on c.id = o.customer_id
join products p on p.id = o.product_id
join orders o2 on o2.id = o.id
join customers c2 on c2.id = o2.customer_id
join products p2 on p2.id = o2.product_id

examples.title: Subqueries nested too deep
examples.sql: select * from (select * from (select * from (select * from (select id from products) a) b) c) d

examples.title: A LIMIT it can't enforce
examples.sql: select id from orders limit all

examples.title: A parse error
examples.sql: select (1

examples.title: The columns public may read
examples.sql: select name, price_cents from products order by price_cents desc limit 5

examples.title: A table public may not read
examples.sql: select * from employee_salaries

examples.title: A column public may not read
examples.sql: select id, category from products

examples.title: A column used only in WHERE
examples.sql: select name from products where category = 'Books'
examples.look: Filtering on a column reveals it too, so every clause is checked.

examples.title: SELECT * where only some columns are allowed
examples.sql: select * from products
examples.look: The reason lists the columns public may read.

examples.title: A CTE named after an allowed table
examples.sql:
with products as (select id, email as name from customers)
select name from products
examples.look: The check sees through the CTE to the customers table it reads.

examples.title: A statement timeout
examples.sql: select count(*) from orders a cross join orders b
examples.look: Allowed, then cancelled after warehouse.statement_timeout_ms (5 s).

examples.title: A database error
examples.sql: select 1 / 0
